name: Rooted Communities
tagline: Neighborhood projects led by the people who live there
who: Community groups, tenant associations, faith groups and small nonprofits with a budget under $1.5 million, working in a neighborhood they are part of.
what: Community gardens, youth programs, neighborhood safety and repair projects, local food access and cultural events, when residents decide what happens and lead the work.
not_fund: Individuals, political campaigns, capital campaigns for buildings, or projects led from outside the neighborhood.
description:
Rooted Communities is our oldest program and still our largest. It backs the people who already know what their block needs and are already doing something about it.

We keep the application short, we fund general operating costs as readily as projects, and we will talk to you before you apply if you want us to.

name: Open Water
tagline: Healthy rivers and a region ready for floods and drought
who: Nonprofits, tribes, watershed councils and public agencies partnering with community groups in the Alder River watershed.
what: River and wetland restoration, flood and drought readiness, clean drinking water in small systems, and science that local people can use to make decisions.
not_fund: Lobbying, litigation, or research without a clear local use.
description:
The Alder River ties the region together, from the Upper Valley headwaters to the estuary at the Coast. Open Water funds the work that keeps it healthy and keeps the towns along it safe as the climate changes.

Most grants run for three years, because rivers move slowly and good restoration takes time.

name: First Chapters
tagline: Every child reading by the end of third grade
who: Libraries, schools, family literacy programs and early-childhood providers serving children from birth to age nine.
what: Tutoring, book access, family reading programs, multilingual early literacy and summer learning.
not_fund: Standardized test preparation, or private schools that charge tuition.
description:
A child who reads well by the end of third grade is far more likely to finish high school. First Chapters funds the people who get books into homes and help families read together, in every language spoken in the region.

We review applications every month. Most decisions take six weeks.

name: Working Futures
tagline: Paid training that leads to a good job
who: By invitation. Workforce partnerships that include employers, community colleges or unions, and a community organization.
what: Paid apprenticeships, pre-apprenticeship programs, wraparound support such as childcare and transport, and pathways for people returning from prison.
not_fund: Training that is not connected to real job openings.
description:
Working Futures pays for training that people can afford to take, because it pays them while they learn, and that ends with a job that pays enough to live on.

We invite applications after talking with partners. If you think your work fits, write to us; we read every note.

name: Rapid Response
tagline: Small, fast grants when something goes wrong
who: Any group in the region responding to an emergency: a flood, a fire, a plant closing, a sudden loss of funding.
what: Immediate costs: supplies, staff time, emergency rent and food, and the first weeks of recovery.
not_fund: Costs that are already covered by insurance or public aid.
description:
When the river flooded Lowlands in 2024, the first grants went out in four days. Rapid Response exists so that a short form and a phone call can get money to the people already helping.

We decide within ten working days, usually sooner.
